'''Adam Wechsler Wexman's Scanning Crew Deck''' is a [[Dark]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Adam Wechsler]]
* '''Published:''' December 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Cloud City]]
* '''Side:''' [[Dark]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Death Star: Central Core|Premiere-D-deathstarcentralcore.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Wexman's Scanning Crew Deck
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PCC Wexman's Scanning Crew Deck Wechsler.txt |Download]]

== Strategy ==

The Scanning Crew Deck is not an uncommon one. However, since none have yet been posted, I have decided to submit my own. Unlike most other dark decks, this deck is ground-oriented and interrupt- heavy.

== Strategy ==

Start with Mos Eisley so you can guarantee some early force draining. The first card you play should be a Scanning Crew. Aside from delaying your opponent's deployment of good Rebels, Scanning Crew gives you an idea of what else your opponent can play against you. Thus, you'll know when it's safe to deploy a lone character or starship to do some draining on the next turn. Also, Scanning Crew can tell you when it's time to start saving force to play Monnok Lost. Of course, if your Scanning Crews are making your opponents draw lots of cards to get characters, don't hesitate to play Monnok Used if he's low on doubles.

Gravel Storms help take care of the characters that do make it down to Tatooine, and R2-Q2 can be used to find out if your next Gravel Storm will take care of the Undercover Momaw Nadon that your opponent got by you. Gravel Storm can also be used effectively right before initiating a battle, like the time I Gravel Stormed Chewbacca and initiated a battle against Zev Senesca and Figrin D'an.

Putting one of the DS-61 brothers on his matching TIE Fighter will almost guarantee you a winning Tallon Roll, even if your opponent uses a Corellian Slip! Keep your opponent off of Tatooine as long as possible, and if you can get Mosep down, those Scanning Crews can help put all of your opponent's Obi's and Luke's into the Lost Pile. Enemies of this deck: BoShek, What Are You Trying To Push On Us? Not every light side deck contains these cards, though, so in a tournament this deck performs well.
